title: K'inich Janaab' Pakal I (Pakal the Great)
biography: Ajaw of the Maya city-state of Palenque for 68 years. Commissioned spectacular hieroglyphic architecture including the Temple of the Inscriptions, where his famous carved jade-masked sarcophagus was discovered.
internationalConnections: Established diplomatic trade alliances with Tikal, Yaxchilan, and Copán across Mesoamerica.

title: King Gunabharnam Pandaram
biography: Gunabharnam Pandaram's brief ten-year reign under Kotte's suzerainty maintained Jaffna's Hindu culture and local administration. He paid tribute to Parakramabahu VI while preserving northern traditions, exemplifying Jaffna's semi-autonomous status during the mid-15th century.

title: Nebuchadnezzar II the Great
biography: Longest-reigning king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire who restored Babylon to architectural majesty, constructing the Ishtar Gate, the Processional Way, and the legendary Hanging Gardens.
internationalConnections: Conducted military campaigns across the Levant, Egypt, and Tyre.

title: Ashoka the Great
biography: Ashoka was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty, who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE. He promoted the spread of Buddhism across ancient Asia.

sections.heading: Biography
content: After the brutal Kalinga War, Ashoka renounced violence and embraced Buddhism.
He established a welfare state, built hospitals for people and animals, and erected pillars with edicts promoting morality.

title: King Kassapa II
biography: Kassapa II (602–608 CE) ruled for six years, maintaining continuity after Aggabodhi I's long tenure. His reign focused on routine governance: irrigation maintenance, temple endowments, and judicial administration. Chronicles note his piety, suggesting adherence to established Buddhist patronage norms.

title: King Richard I (The Lionheart / Cœur de Lion)
biography: Legendary warrior king of England and Duke of Normandy who led the Third Crusade, capturing Acre and defeating Saladin at the Battle of Arsuf.
internationalConnections: Forged the Treaty of Jaffa with Sultan Saladin, guaranteeing unarmed Christian pilgrims access to Jerusalem.
